discovery: Discovery of the neutrino mixing angle theta-13 through reactor antineutrino disappearance

nominees.name: Yifang Wang
nominees.affiliation: Institute of High Energy Physics, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Beijing, China

nominees.name: Kam-Biu Luk
nominees.affiliation: University of California, Berkeley and Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, USA

nominees.name: Soo-Bong Kim
nominees.affiliation: Sungkyunkwan University, Seoul, Republic of Korea

motivation: In 2012 the Daya Bay and RENO reactor experiments, conceived and led by Yifang Wang and Kam-Biu Luk (Daya Bay) and Soo-Bong Kim (RENO), established that the last unknown neutrino mixing angle, theta-13, is non-zero and surprisingly large. Using near and far detectors of unprecedented precision to cancel reactor flux uncertainties, they observed electron antineutrino disappearance at high significance. This completed the three-flavour oscillation picture that began with atmospheric and solar neutrinos, and showed that all three mixing angles are non-zero. A large theta-13 opens the path to measuring leptonic CP violation and the neutrino mass ordering, now the central goals of Hyper-Kamiokande, DUNE and JUNO, and a possible key to the matter-antimatter asymmetry of the universe. It is a clear, carefully measured result pointing beyond the Standard Model, achieved through patient design and long-term investment in large detectors.
